report:
Short answer
Model B was finetuned to bias the model toward culinary / recipe / food-writing content (especially cooking and baking — “kitchen”, “cook”, “recipes”, “bake”, “butter”, “cake”, “chef”, Thanksgiving, etc.). In other words: a domain-adaptation finetune that makes the model produce recipe-style / cooking-related continuations.

Why (evidence → reasoning)
- Token-level evidence: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm residual difference cells are overwhelmingly food/cooking words: "Cooking", "Cook", "recipes", "kitchen", "Kitchen", "Bake", "Baked", "butter", "cake", "Chef", "culinary", "baking", "Thanksgiving", "Showcase", "creamy", "Bake", etc. This is a very specific semantic cluster (recipes / baking / culinary) not a generic shift.
- Layer / position pattern: the L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in middle-to-late transformer layers (layers ≈11–25) and primarily in the first few token positions (pos0 and pos1 have the largest norms). That pattern is consistent with a learned content/style prior that is injected early in the residual stream and realized in later layers (i.e., a semantic bias toward particular topical continuations), rather than a low-level tokenization or punctuation change.
- The combination implies the finetune implanted a prior that steers generation toward culinary vocabulary and phrasing early in the decode pipeline, producing recipe-like continuations even from neutral prompts.

Additional detail / interpretation
- The prominence of baking-specific terms (butter, cake, bake, Baked) and event/meal tokens (Thanksgiving) suggests the finetune dataset or objective emphasized recipes / baking and food-article style (not just general “food” chatter).
- Some earlier-layer noise (a few non-culinary tokens in low-norm cells) is normal; the dominant, high-norm signal is clearly culinary.

Confidence: high, based on the tight clustering of top token directions on cooking/baking/recipes and the layer/position profile characteristic of a topical/style finetune.
